purpose: Define the complete Crew Blueprint knowledge-base model that joins historical curriculum, current evidence, learner journeys, labor-demand signals, authority boundaries, media, cross-product links, and web-client projections without collapsing source ownership.
product_statement: Crew Blueprint is an evidence-backed learning graph rendered through small learner-facing journeys. It is not a flat 143-course catalog, not V4 source truth, not the clean-sheet prototype, and not a duplicate of Production Atlas.

version_layer.rule: Version presentation is lineage/context. Canonical claim/evidence state comes from the normalized Crew Blueprint graph, not from whichever UI version renders a concept.

semantic_separations: learner navigation simplification != deletion of underlying knowledge
ingestion_and_projection_pipeline: 1. preserve source repository/ref/path/commit or external source provenance
3. classify support strength, applicability, jurisdiction, authority, freshness, and publication state
4. join Roadmapdev demand signals only as curriculum-priority planning evidence
5. resolve course/content lineage and historical versions
6. map canonical content into career lanes, context overlays, Field Skills, career resources, and advanced nodes
7. attach stable Production Atlas links rather than volatile Atlas payload copies
11. record learner interaction state separately from authority and qualification

use: test whether curriculum reflects recurring job-side capability signals
prohibited_use: copying raw employer/pay/opening data into lessons

presentation_architecture.principle: The learner sees a small decision surface while the full graph remains available underneath.

current_v4_state_model.strength: V4 separates lesson completion from last-viewed state and allows assessment retry.
current_v4_state_model.remaining_requirement: Future backend/runtime state must continue separating knowledge completion, assessment, observed practice, and external authorization.

high_safety_content: unsupported external claims blocked or visibly qualified
web_projection: no unsupported inference introduced by rendering

historical_retention.rule: Presentation merge/split/hide decisions never delete historical identity or materially distinct archived bodies without explicit owner-authorized archive action.

known_current_debt.finding: V4 content/source objects remain partly hand-maintained and should be generated from canonical graph state before they are treated as provenance truth.

The generated unsupported view contains many high-safety boundary records. Internal product-policy boundaries and external factual/legal claims need explicit support-state treatment rather than one undifferentiated unsupported bucket.
Some presentation code embeds branch/path assumptions. Cross-product routing should use stable Atlas identifiers/URLs owned by Production Atlas rather than copied repository internals.
PR #57 maps all 143 identities but remains proposed until owner acceptance/merge.
The normalized web payload is specified but not yet generated by a build/runtime service.
MEDIA schema exists and selected visuals are normalized, but sitewide media coverage remains incomplete and safety-critical visuals require review discipline.

next_build_outputs_after_acceptance: sitewide media backlog derived from the instructional-media map
unsupported/external-claim closure queue split from internal policy boundaries
lane/context/deep-node renderer consuming canonical IDs rather than hard-coded catalogs
source/freshness UI based on canonical provenance
release_invariants: Frozen V2 and clean-sheet references remain immutable.
All 143 canonical identities remain accounted for through lineage even if not exposed as peer public courses.
No personal information enters public Crew Blueprint or Production Atlas repositories.
Production Atlas volatile data is linked, not duplicated into static curriculum by default.
Roadmapdev analysis remains advisory until accepted through Crew Blueprint governance.
No course or visual implies qualification merely because it appears later or deeper in a path.
No learner state is interpreted as employer/site authorization.
Every generated client surface can trace rendered content back to canonical IDs and evidence state.
